ratings_why.fun: Gusts feed three payoff families, and Föhn, the Windhover, Mistral and the Wild Hunt cross-wire in ways the builds don't even list, so every board can grow differently.
ratings_why.distinct: Announced makes play order a shop decision that reaches across tribes, and Föhn turning enemy attacks into your engine is unlike any tribe today; Gust alone would be a generic extra attack.

verdict_why: The engine is rich and should keep its heat; one real fix is how Lady High Pressure's cancelled attacks interact with Föhn and with a Sir Vane copy.

points.text: Lady High Pressure's rules don't settle two of the tribe's own combos: the Föhn ruling calls his forced Gusts enemy attacks, so are they the 3 she cancels (each giving you a Gust instead)? And with Sir Vane copying her, are the first 3 cancelled twice, or the first 6?

The Bag-Bearer just hands out a Gust. If giving a Bag of Winds also Announced the unit, the two keywords would meet in the shop and the Bag would become a way to pick your Announced carry after the fact.
The Barometer Clerk's stats branch grows only itself; giving that +1/+1 to the Announced unit instead would tie it into the court and make the 4-Gust threshold a real choice.

Once a board is set, Announced can't move back to a unit already in play, so late turns tend toward not playing anything. One small re-Announce outlet beyond the Helm (a card or spell) would keep the play-order puzzle alive late.

standouts.why: Old Föhn makes the enemy's biggest units power your Windhover, Bristle and Bog folk, the best off-label card in the tribe.
The Thunderhead's 'first time it attacks or Gusts' turns the Crier's forecast into a seating hazard inside your own engine.
Sir Vane copies any tribe's text and can break or extend the Crier line, so he's a different card on every board.

weakest.why: Red Sky at Night is a plain end-of-turn buffer whose only twist is the shared Announced target.
The Bag-Bearer is a delivery card with no decision beyond who gets the Bag.
The Barometer Clerk is filler economy; its stats branch rewards a board that isn't doing the tribe's thing.

flags.note: Up to +20/+20 per fight on each Announced unit, doubled by the Helm and golden; with the Mistral and Wild Hunt kill chain it's the likeliest runaway.
Sir Vane, and golden Vane above all, copying Tier 6 capstones from Tier 5.
Unclear whether Föhn's forced enemy Gusts count among the 3 cancelled attacks, and how two copies stack.
With Sir Vane copying the Thunderhead, two units each 'attack after your other units'; their order isn't said.
